Academic Unit Reviews Policy 
                    Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  4  
 
1. Introduction, Context and Principles 
1.1 Academic unit review is a quality assurance and enhancement process that 
evaluates the quality, currency and strategic alignment of the provision of education 
by an individual academic unit. This includes:  
• the strategic direction of that unit;  
• its teaching, learning and assessment strategies;  
• its research objectives and activities;  
• its provision of taught and research programmes, including those 
programmes that are provided fully or in part through third-party 
arrangements2; and  
• its provision of services to industry, the region and society in general (‘third 
mission’).  
Academic unit review is a core part of the University’s quality assurance 
infrastructure and is based on the internationally accepted review model outlined 
inter alia within the Standards and Guidelines for Quality Assurance in the European 
Higher Education Area (2015). Academic unit review is conducted on a five-yearly 
cycle and will normally be undertaken on a faculty or departmental basis but may 
also consider smaller units within individual faculties or departments, as 
necessary3.  
 
1.2 This policy sets out the basis for the University’s conduct of academic unit reviews. It 
is grounded in the principles set out in the University Reviews Policy, including: 
• Compliance with Irish and international obligations and requirements, both 
statutory and non-statutory. 
• Cognisance of the SETU Quality Framework document, the Standards and 
Guidelines for Quality Assurance in the European Higher Education Area 
(2015) and relevant policies and guidelines developed by Quality and 
Qualifications Ireland (QQI). 
• Awareness of emerging national and international developments, legislative 
or otherwise, regarding the provision of education. 
• Regard for stakeholder expectations, including students and staff of SETU 
and third-party providers involved in the delivery of programmes leading to 
SETU awards, employers, industry, external bodies such as with professional 
 
2 The term ‘third-party arrangement’ is used to denote any relationship between SETU and another provider of 
higher education or further education and training for the purpose of programme delivery and/or awarding. 
The use of the term in this policy relates only to providers involved in the delivery of programmes leading to 
SETU awards. This includes, for example, relationships with collaborative providers, linked providers and co-
delivery relationships. 
3 Note: For clarity, ‘academic unit’ will be used throughout this policy and accompanying procedure to refer to 
the unit undergoing academic unit review. An academic unit may be a faculty, a department or another sub-
unit responsible for the development and delivery of programmes.

Academic Unit Reviews Policy 
                    Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  5  
 
statutory and regulatory bodies (PSRB)s, other educational institutions and 
the State as a whole. 
• Commitment to continuous improvement as part of a cycle of periodic 
academic unit review of the University’s provision. 
• Alignment (insofar as is practicable) with PSRB processes and requirements. 
 2. Purpose 
2.1 This policy details how the University intends to meet its statutory obligations 
regarding internal quality review of its academic units and their education strategies, 
management and provision, including, but not limited to: 
• 
Ensuring that each award it makes is an award that is included within the 
National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ) (Qualifications and Quality 
Assurance [Education and Training] Act 2012 (as amended), s. 43 (3)). This 
is, in part, demonstrated by the review process’ consideration of the 
alignment of programmes and their learning outcomes with SETU award 
standards, which, in turn, have been aligned with the NFQ. 
• 
Ensuring, in respect of each award made by the University that is recognised 
within the NFQ, that each learner achieving an award has achieved the 
standard of knowledge, skill and competence associated with the award 
level (Qualifications and Quality Assurance [Education and Training] Act 
2012 (as amended), s. 43 (6), (8)). This is, in part, demonstrated, by the 
review process’ reflection upon the assessment strategies and 
methodologies used by the academic unit in question, as well as its 
consideration of analyses of learner achievement. 
• 
Establishing and undergoing reviews of the effectiveness of its quality 
assurance procedures and its procedures for access, transfer and 
progression (Qualifications and Quality Assurance [Education and Training] 
Act 2012 (as amended), s. 28, s. 34, s. 56, s. 57). This is, in part, 
demonstrated by the review process’ consideration of the implementation 
of the SETU quality assurance infrastructure, including procedures for 
access, transfer and progression and for the provision of student supports, 
by and within the academic unit.  
The policy demonstrates the University’s regard to the Sector Specific Statutory 
Quality Assurance Guidelines developed by QQI for Designated Awarding Bodies 
(2016), which outline the expectation that Designated Awarding Bodies conduct 
periodic reviews of study programmes. It also supports the University in 
demonstrating alignment with the Joint-Sectoral Protocol between Designated 
Awarding Bodies and Quality and Qualifications Ireland for the Inclusion of 
Qualifications within the National Framework of Qualifications (2022), which, in 
turn, demonstrates that the University has met the requirements for inclusion of 
awards within the NFQ (s. 55B of the 2012 Act (as amended)).

Academic Unit Reviews Policy 
                    Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  6  
 
2.2 This policy sets out the stages and outcomes of the academic unit review process, 
and the responsibilities of the University, the relevant academic unit and other 
relevant stakeholders involved in carrying out academic unit review and responding 
to its outcomes. 
 
This policy further creates the basis for the University to develop a schedule of 
academic unit reviews or to conduct reviews of specific programmes or suites of 
programmes outside of that schedule where a need to do so is identified. In cases 
where a review of programmes is required, the review process will be guided by 
section 4 below, adapted as necessary. 
 
2.3 Finally, this policy seeks to ensure that appropriate action is taken following the 
conduct of academic unit review and that review processes, their actions and 
consequent action taken by academic units support a cycle of continuous 
improvement in the University’s education provision. 
3. Scope 
3.1  This policy applies to all of the University’s academic units and all SETU students 
and staff. This includes students and staff of third-party providers involved in the 
delivery of programmes leading to SETU awards. Staff and students are required to 
engage with the policy as necessary and are expected to participate in and 
contribute to reviews as appropriate. 
4. Policy 
4.1  Academic unit review incorporates the review of all activity within an academic 
unit, including strategic direction of that unit; its teaching, learning and assessment 
strategies; its research objectives and activities; its development of the relevant 
discipline(s), its management and provision of the taught and research programmes 
within its portfolio; and its provision of services to industry, the region and society 
in general (‘third mission’).  
This includes programmes leading to SETU awards that are provided through third-
party arrangements with other providers of education and training, both nationally 
and internationally.   
4.2 Review Objectives 
Academic unit review provides a means for the University (and its individual 
academic units) to:  
• 
assure the University of the currency, coherence, strategic alignment and 
quality of its education provision; research activity; teaching, learning and 
assessment strategies; the management and delivery of its programme 
portfolio; and its contribution of services to industry, the region and society

Academic Unit Reviews Policy 
                    Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  7  
 
in general (‘third mission’), and to facilitate it to benchmark itself against 
that of peer educational institutions both in Ireland and internationally;  
• 
ensure that academic delivery within an academic unit is reviewed and 
revised in line with contemporary pedagogical and discipline-area best 
practice;  
• 
elicit and respond to feedback from University constituents and 
stakeholders and align its academic delivery; research activity; and teaching, 
learning and assessment with the needs of industry, learners and society 
generally; 
• 
maintain public confidence in the University’s provision of education and 
research activity; 
• 
reflect upon the governance, management and operation of the University’s 
academic delivery with a view to highlighting and disseminating good 
practice as well as identifying key opportunities, challenges and weaknesses, 
and implementing actions that will support development and improvement; 
• 
consider the effectiveness of quality assurance procedures for academic 
unit review. 
 
4.3 Academic Unit Review Schedule 
Academic unit reviews are scheduled and conducted in accordance with the 
University’s statutory obligations. Where possible and appropriate, the Office of 
the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning, will endeavour to 
schedule academic unit review processes to support their alignment or appropriate 
sequencing with related statutory and regulatory processes for accreditation or 
approval by the relevant PSRB.  
 
4.4 Key Review Stages 
The key stages in each academic unit review process are: 
a. Agreement of a timeline for the individual academic unit review process between 
the relevant head(s) of the academic unit (and, where they are not a member of 
the Executive Management Team, the key executive(s) in the academic unit) and 
the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning. 
Each review process will be in alignment with the overall academic unit review 
schedule established by the Joint Quality Committee; 
b. Engagement by the academic unit’s staff and students, as well as relevant 
internal and external stakeholders, in a self-evaluation process;  
c. Preparation of a self-evaluation report by the academic unit through a self-
evaluation committee; 
d. Review of the self-evaluation report (as part of a broader engagement process, 
typically including a site visit and meetings with relevant internal and external

Academic Unit Reviews Policy 
                    Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  8  
 
stakeholders) by a peer review group, who are appointed and approved by the 
Joint Quality Committee; 
e. Preparation of a peer review group report, to include recommendations of the 
peer review group; 
f. Consideration of the peer review group report by the academic unit (including 
the unit’s executive lead) and drafting of the academic unit’s response to the 
report through the executive lead; 
g. Development of a quality enhancement plan by the academic unit arising from 
the report; 
h. Consideration of the outcome of the review process, including any 
recommendations, and approval of the quality enhancement plan by the 
University through Academic Council and (through the Joint Quality Committee) 
Governing Body4; 
i. Publication of the peer review group report on the University website to ensure 
transparency and dissemination of good practice and to promote public 
confidence; 
j. Ongoing monitoring by the University of the quality enhancement plan’s 
implementation by the academic unit through submission of an annual update 
on implementation to the Joint Quality Committee. 
4.5 Review Guidelines 
Academic units undergoing academic unit review will be supported by guidelines 
for the conduct of review processes, which will be maintained by the Office of the 
Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning. 
4.6 Self-evaluation Process and Report 
A self-evaluation process based on the principles of constructive criticism, open and 
honest reflection on current practice and formulation of recommendations for 
improvement of provision, is central to the academic unit review process.  
 
Responsibility to produce self-evaluation reports rests with academic unit 
management. To support consistency of approach across the University, the Office 
of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning will develop and 
maintain a template for self-evaluation reports. 
4.7 Peer Review Group Composition 
The peer review group will include an appropriate balance of expertise and 
experience and will comprise a suitably qualified chair, an appropriate number of 
external academic and professional representatives relevant to the discipline area, 
an external student representative, and a secretary, who is responsible for drafting 
the peer review group report, from the Office of the Vice President for Academic 
 
4 Where substantive matters of note need to be considered by Governing Body, these will be reported to 
Governing Body by the Joint Quality Committee and/or Academic Council.

Academic Unit Reviews Policy 
                    Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  9  
 
Affairs, Teaching and Learning. Regard will be had to international representation 
and gender balance in the establishment of peer review groups. 
5. Responsibilities 
5.1 Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning 
 
5.1.1 The organisation and operational management of academic unit reviews is the 
responsibility of the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching 
and Learning, in consultation with the management of the relevant academic 
unit. 
 
5.1.2 Peer review group members will be provided with appropriate briefing and 
training by the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and 
Learning to ensure their familiarity with the University’s context and that of the 
academic unit under review. 
5.2 Joint Quality Committee 
The Joint Quality Committee is responsible for the formation of the academic unit 
reviews policy, for approving the schedule of academic unit reviews, for approving 
and appointing the composition of academic unit peer review groups, for ensuring 
that academic unit reviews are taking place and being reported on, and for 
ensuring that reviews are being completed and their outcomes implemented. The 
Committee is also responsible for making recommendations to Governing Body on 
relevant approvals. 
5.3 Executive Management Team 
The relevant Executive is responsible for considering the outcome of the review, 
drafting an executive response to the recommendations (which will focus on the 
financial impact of the quality enhancement plan), and submitting the quality 
enhancement plan for approval to Governing Body (through the Joint Quality 
Committee) and Academic Council.  
5.4 Academic Council 
Academic Council is responsible for the approval of the outcomes of academic unit 
reviews – to include any recommendations, as well as the quality enhancement 
plan – and monitoring the plan’s implementation by the academic unit. 
5.5 Unit under Review 
The unit under review is responsible for undertaking a comprehensive self-
evaluation exercise of its activities, ensuring that all relevant stakeholders, internal 
and external to the unit, are involved in and/or consulted on the process. It will 
then record the process and its outcomes in a self-evaluation report. The unit 
under review is also responsible for ensuring that a representative selection of

internal and external stakeholders is available to meet with the peer review group 
during the site visit.  
Following the production of the review report, the unit under review will develop a 
quality enhancement plan, setting out how it intends responding to and 
implementing any recommendations proposed by the peer review group. As 
outlined above, the unit’s implementation of the quality enhancement plan will be 
monitored by the University. 
5.6 Final Approval of Review Outcomes 
The final approval of the outcomes of all academic unit reviews, as well as 
monitoring of the related quality enhancement plans, is undertaken by Governing 
Body (through the Joint Quality Committee) and Academic Council.

7. Review of Policy 
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date, and/or as soon as possible 
following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
8. Author 
The author of this policy is the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, 
Teaching and Learning. Any feedback or issues arising on implementation of this policy 
should be communicated to the policy author. The policy author is responsible for 
ensuring that the Policy Owner is aware of these comments when reviewing the policy.
